title: FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint (umbrella)
creator: Talia Benson
description:
Umbrella issue for the Serving Runtime “FP8/INT8 kernel benchmarking sprint”.

Goal
Quantify + improve performance of quantization-friendly execution paths (FP8 + INT8) across top hosted models and primary GPU SKUs. Deliver a defensible benchmark report, land a small set of high-confidence improvements (kernel + scheduler + defaults), and leave behind repeatable automation (harness, dashboards, gating).

Success metrics (sprint-level)
- Benchmark report is publishable internally and “defensible” for enterprise prospects: methodology documented; environments pinned; results reproducible.
- Coverage: top hosted model families + realistic traffic shapes (prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy; streaming vs non-streaming) across A100 + H100/H200 + L40S (MI300X optional if available).
- Performance deltas from landed changes are measurable and attributable (kernel ID/shape tracing; per-phase timings).
- Guardrails: INT8/FP8 drift checks vs FP16 baseline on a small prompt set; clear rollback and fallback criteria.
- Automation: nightly quant perf-canary with regression thresholds + allowlists; dashboard panels with tags (model/GPU/runtime commit/quant mode/kernel).

Scope notes
- In scope: quantized GEMM/attention kernels (FP8/INT8), kernel auto-selection behavior, KV cache interaction points, scheduler policies affecting prefill/decode interleaving + batching.
- Non-goals: customer-facing pricing/packaging changes; broad product/UX work; large model quality research beyond existing correctness/quality guardrails.

Milestones / timeline
Week 1 (Sep 29 – Oct 4)
- Finalize benchmark spec + workload presets.
- Pin perf-lab environment (driver/CUDA/container digest) and document setup.
- Land harness changes (streaming chat scenario; consistent tagging + artifact format).
- Collect baselines (FP16 vs FP8 vs INT8) for top hosted models.

Week 2 (Oct 7 – Oct 17)
- Run full matrix and investigate anomalies.
- Land targeted optimizations + safe config defaults (kernel selection fixes; H100/H200 tuning; scheduler batch caps for quant decode).
- Add dashboards and perf-canary gating with thresholds/allowlists.
- Publish sprint report + ADR updates and define follow-up roadmap.

Risks / watchouts
- Perf lab noise / contention: must enforce dedicated nodes, lock GPU clocks where allowed, and record clock/power metadata per run.
- Kernel selection opacity: without logging of chosen kernel + shapes, we can’t attribute deltas; treat logging improvements as a blocker for “defensible” reporting.
- Tail latency vs throughput tradeoffs: scheduler batching changes may improve p95 but regress throughput in decode-heavy scenarios; report both and make defaults conservative.
- Correctness: INT8 (and some FP8) paths can introduce drift; do not ship new defaults without drift checks and a clear fallback policy.

Deliverables checklist
- [ ] Updated benchmark harness supporting streaming TTFT/TPOT and phase breakdowns (prefill vs decode).
- [ ] Standard experiment matrix generator + workload presets for top hosted models.
- [ ] Pinned/reproducible perf-lab environment (container digest + driver/CUDA versions) + runbook.
- [ ] Kernel selection + quant-mode tracing spans/events with shapes and kernel IDs.
- [ ] Dashboard panels and queries for quant perf trends by model/GPU/quant/kernel.
- [ ] Perf-canary nightly job with robust comparator + regression thresholds and notifications.
- [ ] Written sprint report: baseline, deltas, anomaly explanations, recommended defaults, follow-ups.

Related external signal (context)
- SUP-6193: customer-reported latency regression on INT8 variant after a runtime update (workaround: pin/rollback). Use as a sanity check that our canary would have caught it.
- SUP-6194: intermittent output quality issues suspected from FP8 path (pending investigation). Ensure sprint guardrails explicitly cover this class of regression.

Notes
- This umbrella tracks planning, cross-team alignment, and milestone completion. Individual implementation tasks should be tracked in the sub-issues above, with PR links and acceptance criteria kept there. Use this issue for weekly status and “go/no-go” on shipping quant changes in runtime-1.18.
